method: synthetic 320x240 frames through the real pipeline (analyzeColorBlobs -> _applyDualResult -> updateCameraLook -> VRController); head turn modelled physically: both boxes shift together in small steps, the far box leaves the frame, a foreign blob of its hue appears near the frame centre
symptom_verbatim: Сейчас если взгляд увести в сторону то он очень быстро возвращается куда то в центр и я не пойму почему.

hypotheses.pseudo_markers: CONFIRMED (mechanism differs from the guess): the detector does not lose the real marker, it ADDS a foreign blob of the same hue, and the pair angle was the mean of one honest and one alien delta — the mean always pulls toward the frame centre because each delta is measured from that marker's own calibrated spot
hypotheses.loss_counted_on_first_marker: REFUTED: with one box visible found=true / fresh=true, hold and edge-turn keep working; the 4 s return-to-centre needs BOTH markers gone and is not the cause

before.amplifier: main.js: camWasLost && jump > 8 -> camSnapPending -> second frame -> hard re-anchor camSmooth.yaw = t.yaw (no smoothing) — a false blob could snap the aim instantly
before.formula: yaw = mean(delta_left, delta_right) with each delta measured from that marker's own calibration

rules: both visible and deltas agree within 6 deg -> mean as before (pairState 'pair')
both visible but deltas disagree -> trust-based single side, NO mean (pairState 'conflict'), loser loses 0.45 trust/frame
both masks hit the same object (centres < 4% of the frame apart) -> one side (pairState 'same')
one visible -> it leads alone (pairState 'single'), unchanged
blob smaller than max(40 px, 8% of calibrated) -> not a marker at all (pairState 'tiny')
jump limiter: 260 deg/s, floor 8 deg, cap 30 deg per processed frame (processing interval is 90-170 ms by tier)
after >900 ms without a marker: honest re-entry is accepted without the speed limit, but only if the next frame agrees within 3 deg (two-frame confirmation)
trust is required only when a competitor exists, so a lone visible marker can never freeze permanently

dual: pair shift gives a new angle
losing right leaves left leading (lastLostMarker right)
losing both keeps the last angle
alien blob does not pull the gaze to the centre (state conflict, trust right -> 0)
when the pair agrees again the count is by two markers (state pair)
tiny blob is ignored, big blob leads

after a long loss the angle is accepted by the second frame
dual_and_space: pair shift gives a new angle
losing both keeps the last angle
at +-5 deg both markers are expected inside the frame, both used, neither missing
a raspberry blob left of the orange marker is a foreign object (order/separation invariant)
a hue that cannot be inside the frame is ignored entirely
the reflected blob does not pull the gaze to the centre
steadily turning 20 deg/s is measured as 21 deg/s
tiny blob ignored, normal blob leads
an instant 33 deg jump is rejected; accepted on the second agreeing frame
while markers are lost the gaze keeps turning at the recent head speed

field_notes: if conflicts appear with both markers clearly visible and stable, raise DUAL_PAIR_GATE_DEG (6 deg ~ 26 px at fx=251 px / 65 deg FOV)
trust is not persisted across rides: a fresh calibration resets it to 1.0
remaining: not verified on real footage, only synthetically (headless SwiftShader); the tuning values (6 deg / 260 dps / 900 ms) are geometric estimates and may need one field iteration
max reachable yaw in the synthetic path is about +-32 deg (frame width), real range depends on camera FOV and marker placement
report_status: two rounds: (1) pair no longer averages conflicting deltas, (2) spatial + velocity model of the pair (2026-10-17)

spatial_velocity_model.why: markers are fixed in the world: their order, separation and calibrated spots never change, and the head angle has a measurable speed over the last seconds — so most 'unexpected' detections can be rejected by physics instead of by trust heuristics
rules: pair separation is an invariant: observed (right raw yaw - left raw yaw) must stay within 6 deg of the calibrated value, so 'raspberry left of orange' is impossible by construction
each marker's expected position = its calibrated raw yaw + predicted head angle (last accepted angle + yawRate * dt, dt capped at 0.35 s)
a detection whose expected position is outside the frame (>halfFOV + 4 deg + speed slack) is a foreign object: the hue is ignored entirely ('impossible')
an accepted angle must match the model (<= 5-25 deg residual and <= 260 deg/s step); anything else needs a second agreeing frame within 3 deg / 600 ms
when a marker that must be visible is missing while the other leads, the state is 'occluded' (substitutes cannot pass the separation invariant)
while markers are off-frame the gaze keeps moving at the recent head speed (decay ~0.6 s, cap +15 deg), in the same direction only
